description: Murder, dismemberment, a mummy and revenge: the cycle of Osiris and Set founds Egyptian kingship and the hope of a life after death.

hero.hook: A brother kills the king and cuts his body into fourteen pieces. A sister puts him back together. A son takes revenge. All of Egypt comes out of that crime.

blocks.text: The cycle of **Osiris** and **Set** is the great story of ancient Egypt. It is not only a family tragedy. It is the fight between order ([[Ma'at]], harmony) and barren chaos.

Through the murder, the dismemberment and the resurrection of Osiris, the Egyptians thought through kingship, the fertility of the Nile and life after death. Every living pharaoh was a **Horus**. Every dead king became an **Osiris**.

**Osiris** is a king who brings civilization. With **Isis**, his sister and his wife, he teaches farming and law. His brother **Set**, god of the desert and of violence, hates him. At a banquet, Set shows off a magnificent chest: he will give it to whoever fits inside perfectly.

blocks.caption: Osiris with green skin: not death, but plants coming back to life

blocks.text: Set has secretly taken Osiris's measurements. He makes him lie down, locks the chest, seals it with lead and throws it into the Nile. Later, when Isis finds the body, Set cuts it into **14 pieces** and scatters them across the valley. Without an intact body, there is no peace in the afterlife.
Osiris is often painted green. The color does not stand for rot. It stands for rebirth, like the fields after the Nile flood.

**Isis**, a great sorceress, sets out to find the fragments. Helped by her sister Nephthys and by the god [[Anubis]], she raises a shrine at every spot where she recovers a piece. One problem remains: the phallus has been eaten by the [[Oxyrhynchus]] fish. Isis shapes a replacement.

blocks.caption: Isis with her wings spread: the breath that revives Osiris

blocks.text: By gathering the pieces and wrapping them in linen strips, Isis and Anubis create the **first mummy**. With a beat of her wings, Isis breathes a short life back into Osiris. That is when she conceives **Horus**, the heir who will restore order.
Some texts say the tears Isis shed during her search were so plentiful that the Egyptians saw in them the mythical origin of the yearly Nile flood.

Raised in secret in the marshes of [[Khemmis]], **Horus** grows up in the form of a falcon. As an adult he claims the throne before the court of the gods, presided over by [[Ra]]. The conflict with Set lasts for decades: duels, tricks, wounds. Horus loses an eye. Set loses his fertility.

blocks.caption: The eye of Horus (the Wedjat): wholeness won back from chaos

blocks.text: The eye, put back together by [[Thoth]], becomes the symbol of healing and protection. The gods hand down their verdict: Set is condemned to serve, above all by fighting the serpent [[Apophis]] on the solar barque. Horus is crowned. From then on every pharaoh will be a “living Horus.”

Mummified, Osiris can no longer reign on earth. He becomes ruler of the **Amenti**, the kingdom of the dead. Under his gaze comes the **weighing of the heart**, described in [[The Book of the Dead]]. The heart of the dead person is set on a scale against the feather of Ma'at.

If the heart is light, the dead person is “true of voice” and enters the eternity of Osiris. If it is heavy with sins, the monster [[Ammit]] devours it: total oblivion. King and farmer are judged by the same standard. Horus handles the present. Osiris takes care of what comes after.

The myth of **Osiris** and **Set** founds three pillars of Egypt: kingship (the living Horus), mummification (an intact body for the afterlife) and the hope of justice after death under the gaze of Osiris.
